newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Int'l postpones start-up till January.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Int'l postpones start-up till January.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines will postpone its return to commercial service until mid-to-late January, spokesman Rob Kulat said Wednesday.
Kiwi said it plans to resume commercial flights with eight of its 15 planes and 450 to 550 of its 1,200 furloughed workers.
The low-cost airline declared Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September and suspended operations in October.
Kiwi previously planned to resume flying before Christmas, but decided to postpone service until January since most travelers already have reservations for holiday travel, Kulat said.
"The prime selling season for Christmas flying has passed. And the period after New Year's is always slow," Kulat said.
Until commercial operations resume, Kiwi will continue to fly charter services. The airline may also fly some routes under contract for another commercial carrier, Kulat said.

Kiwi said it has financing in place to resume operations. The airline received a $5 million financing commitment from an investor group called Wasatch Co, which has been approved by the U.S. Bankrutpcy Court in Newark, N.J.
